html:
SMTO-API-0007 — Your account isn't allowed to do this

GUID: 79d9ab81-bce3-4e6b-a91e-cb52c02ee97d
Slug: api-access-denied
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO knows who you are but turned down this request. The action may need an administrator account, this page's security check may have expired, or you may need to change your password first.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload this page and try the action once more. A page left open for a long time can carry an expired security check, which SMTO refuses until the page reloads.
  2. If SMTO takes you to the Account page, set a new password in its Password section first. SMTO blocks other actions until a required password change is done.
  3. If What the server reported mentions admin, ask the person who manages SMTO to do this for you or to give your account administrator access. Some settings and actions are limited to administrator accounts.

What success looks like

  • The action completes while you're signed in with your intended account.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't sign in with someone else's account, or move the task to a different Gateway or computer, just to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO, Gateway or remote endpoint returned HTTP 403 (for example the portal's admin_required, csrf_rejected or password_change_required) and no more specific registered cause applied.

What this means

  • The remote API client or generic HTTP boundary reports access denial, including status 403 when no more specific registered cause applies. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • The remote API client or generic HTTP boundary reports access denial, including status 403 when no more specific registered cause applies.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected identity, resource and authorization scope; denial is not proof of an expired login.

How to fix it

  • Check the reported reason: admin_required means the route needs an admin role; csrf_rejected means a missing or stale X-SMTO-CSRF token or a cross-origin request (reload the page); password_change_required means the account must change its password at /account first. For CLI calls, confirm the --portal-username account and that required agreements were accepted; do not bypass access controls.
  • Use the intended authorized identity and scope; do not bypass access controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorized identity has the required scope without bypassing access controls.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
